chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from Maʿmar ibn Yaḥyā, from Dāwūd al-Zujājī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
If a woman was menstruating and then became pure before sunset, she prays ẓuhr and ʿaṣr. And if she becomes pure during the night, she prays maghrib and the later ʿishāʾ.

key_terms.الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ: the later night salat (prayer), meaning ʿishāʾ
key_terms.غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, marking the end of the daytime prayer period mentioned here
key_terms.فَطَهُرَتْ: then she became pure from menstruation

ai.seo_question: What prayers must a menstruating woman make up if she becomes pure before sunset or during the night?
ai.summary: This hadith states the prayer ruling for a menstruating woman who becomes pure before the end of a prayer period. If she becomes pure before sunset, she performs ẓuhr and ʿaṣr; if she becomes pure during the night, she performs maghrib and ʿishāʾ. It is a jurisprudential text concerning ritual purity and the obligation of salat (prayer).
